Controls Overview

MelonUI includes controls for displaying information, handling input and arranging pages. The following pages describe how to use each control in C# and MXML, with examples of the output.

Using Controls in C#

The C# examples use these namespaces:

Each example creates a control variable. Add it to Children on a page, or Elements on the window. MXML automatically resolves core types. Examples using App bindings refer to the SettingsModel class in the Data Binding guide.

Pages

  • MUIPage
    • The MUIPage class is used to group UI elements into a page. You can add elements in C# through Children, or use MXML to load the page from a file.

Text and Input

  • TextBlock
    • The TextBlock control displays text in the console. It supports word wrapping, text alignment, and inline colors, making it useful for labels, descriptions, and status messages.
  • TextBox
    • The TextBox control allows users to enter and edit text. You can use it for single-line input, multiline input, or hidden input such as a password.
  • ColorPicker
    • The ColorPicker control allows users to edit the red, green and blue values of a color. It shows the original color alongside the current color, so changes can be previewed before they are saved.
  • RgbColorPicker
    • The RgbColorPicker class provides the ColorPicker control under a name that makes its RGB behavior explicit. It uses the same properties, keyboard controls and events.
  • FilePicker
    • The FilePicker control allows users to browse for a file or directory. It keeps its own current directory, so using the picker does not change the working directory of your application.

Buttons and Menus

  • Button
    • The Button control displays an action that the user can select. When the button is activated, it calls the method assigned to OnPressed.
  • ButtonPanel
    • The ButtonPanel control arranges buttons into an action bar. Buttons that do not fit are placed in an overflow menu, so the panel can still be used in a smaller console window.
  • OptionsMenu
    • The OptionsMenu control displays a list of choices. Each choice is a MenuItem containing its label, callback and enabled state.
  • OverflowMenu
    • The OverflowMenu class is an OptionsMenu that displays actions from a list of buttons. ButtonPanel uses it automatically when some of its buttons do not fit.

Displaying Information

  • ProgressBar
    • The ProgressBar control displays progress for an operation. It can show a percentage and label, or use a loading animation when you do not know how much work remains.
  • WorkLog
    • The WorkLog control displays the progress of multiple jobs. Each job is a WorkItem with its own label, status, item counts and running time.
  • Waveform
    • The Waveform control displays peak amplitudes supplied by your application. It can also highlight how far playback has progressed through the data.
  • Line
    • The Line control draws a line between two points inside its own area. It can be used for dividers or simple horizontal, vertical and diagonal drawing.
  • FPSCounter
    • The FPSCounter control shows how many frames the window is actually presenting. It subscribes to the window when attached and removes that subscription when detached.

Layout Containers

  • GridContainer
    • The GridContainer control divides its area into rows and columns. Each row can have a different number of columns, allowing you to build layouts without assigning a position to every control.
  • QueueContainer
    • The QueueContainer control displays the first visible element in a queue, with a small stack behind it to show that more elements are waiting.

Other Controls

You can also build a custom UIElement, or use the optional shader controls. The output examples are plain text, so they do not show the color of a rendered frame.
